content:
carla-support: FYI customer ArcadiaApps opened a high-priority ticket — they're seeing bursts of 403s and higher p99 latency since 08:24 UTC. They say requests that should hit their Dedicated EU pool are being served by hosted US and billed accordingly. sample_req=req_0a1b2c3

ben-sre: Got it — looking at routing logs now. do we have the routing decision for that req id?

alice-eng: I pulled the router trace for req_0a1b2c3:
```
router.trace: time=2026-03-17T08:24:12Z req=req_0a1b2c3 org=arcadia region_hint=eu-west-1 desired_pool=dedicated-eu decision=hosted-us fallback_reason=DEDICATED_UNAVAILABLE
```
carla-support: The customer insists dedicated pool was healthy (no scale events) — they've got reserved capacity. They pointed at pool id ded-eu-42.

kevin-platform: Two quick checks: 1) auth audience mismatch can cause 403s when going to hosted (hosted expects audience=hosted-api, dedicated expects audience=dedicated-api). 2) pinning keys/TTL race can cause misbinding to default fallback pool.

maria-support: Customer pasted this error from their side: `{"error":"Forbidden","code":403,"msg":"aud mismatch: token audience hosted-api != expected dedicated-api"}`

ben-sre: That matches — when a request falls back to hosted we return 403 if token audience doesn't match the hosted validator. but why did it fall back? checking pool health and routing metrics...

alice-eng: quick grep of the cache writer around 08:23:50 shows a key write with wrong suffix: `pin:d:org:arcadia:region:eu -> ded-eu-42:us` because locale parsing returned `us` in one code path. snippet:
```
[08:23:50] pin-store: set(pin:d:org:arcadia:region:eu) = "ded-eu-42:us" ttl=300
```
ben-sre: omg. that explains the cross-region routing. source likely a string split bug where `region` field got overwritten by last-inserted geo tag.

kevin-platform: Repro steps I'm running locally:
1) create pin with `region=eu` and pool ded-eu-42
2) simulate concurrent pin-refresh (cron) and a fallback write from older host
3) observe key occasionally written with `:us` suffix

kevin-platform: Repro'd it in staging with a small race. Root cause: pin-refresh handler uses `last_known_geo` from request meta when building key suffix; when that field is empty it falls back to `global_default` which used to be `us`. code path introduced during rollout of 2026-02-18.

maria-support: Customer also reported spike in billing to hosted in the same window. can we estimate hosted tokens served?

ben-sre: Telemetry shows ~17k tokens served from hosted for org arcadia between 08:24-08:35 UTC. sending breakdown to ops.

oncall-bot: Incident NOTE: created incident INC-2026-342 routing-misbind-arcadia by ben-sre at 08:43 UTC.

alice-eng: Immediate mitigation: patch to pin-write to prefer explicit region in the request and to disallow fallback suffix. rolling to prod now as `hotfix/routing-pin-guard`.

kevin-platform: Patch includes:
```
- ensure pin_key = f"pin:d:org:{org}:region:{explicit_region}"  # don't use last_known_geo
- add CAS on write to prevent overwrite by fallback process
- log-on-foreign-suffix write and alert
```

ben-sre: I've toggled a temporary rule to prefer dedicated pools for orgs with active reserved capacity while we finish the patch (force-route=dedicated for org:arcadia).

maria-support: Customer confirmed they see successful requests again ~08:50 UTC and 403s dropped. they're watching for billing reconciliation.

carla-support: Can we create a billing adjustment ticket? they were billed for hosted usage for traffic that should've been on their reserved pool.

kevin-platform: Yes — I'll open a billing ops ticket and attach telemetry. action items: patch rollout (alice), billing ticket (kevin), postmortem (ben).

alice-eng: Patch rolled to all regions at 09:02 UTC. I added a temporary log filter to flag any `pin:*` writes containing `:us` suffix outside of US regions.

ben-sre: Postmortem draft outline: root cause = pin key race + fallback writer using default geo. impact = auth 403s + cross-region latency + ~17k hosted tokens billed. mitigation = hotfix + force-route + billing credit. follow-ups = add e2e test for pin-refresh race, harden audience validation messaging, add metric for foreign-pool-writes.

maria-support: Customer asked for a short writeup to send to their security/compliance team explaining the auth 403s — I'll draft and share.

carla-support: thanks everyone. please post postmortem link here when ready. :thumbsup:

kevin-platform: billing ticket BT-778 opened and linked to INC-2026-342. attaching hosted token counts and request ids.

ben-sre: will schedule 1hr blameless postmortem this week. closing incident once postmortem published.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-342 status: resolved (mitigated).

carla-support: marking customer ticket as "mitigated" and letting ArcadiaApps know we are doing billing reconciliation and full postmortem.

alice-eng: TL;DR for docs: pinging should always write region-explicit keys, never derive suffix from fallthrough fields. I'll update docs + add new unit tests.

maria-support: Arcadia replied: "Thanks — we appreciate the quick response. Please keep us posted on billing."

ben-sre: closing notes: if you see similar pattern (403 + hosted billing spike), check `pin:*` writes for unexpected suffixes and routing.trace for reason=DEDICATED_UNAVAILABLE.
